Useful statuses let the department tell the difference between a resource that can accept work and a resource that is already doing something. Open the department menu and custom statuses. The page separates unit status sets, personnel actions, and personnel staffing levels. Unit status sets describe vehicles, apparatus, or field resources. Personnel actions describe what a person is doing. Staffing describes whether that person is available.

ResGrid offers starting templates for ambulance, fire, law enforcement,
search and rescue, general response, disaster response, security, industrial fleets, and logistics. Pick the one that fits the resource's actual lifecycle. We choose search and rescue. Name the set training SAR field team and rename searching to searching assigned area. Templates pre-fill options. They do not save the set. You can review labels, colors, and ordering before clicking add. The saved set contains eight options.
A security company can start from security and use on-patrol and investigating. An industrial team can use fleet and equipment states such as maintenance. A mobile response team can use a reviewed response lifecycle. A wildland contractor can use staging and response states appropriate to its crews and apparatus. Inspect an options base type. Searching has the meaning of actively searching an assigned area, sector, or grid. A clearer button label can preserve that meaning.
Using none creates an informational state without that system meaning. A label that says ready should not be assigned an unavailable meaning, and an attractive green button is not evidence of readiness. Review color contrast and use meaningful text so members do not have to rely on color alone. This build exposed an option edit issue. These controls express different requirements. The detail supplies a destination, such as an incident. The note supplies context. The location requirement supplies a position, where supported by the client. A search team might record the assigned area and team accountability. A security patrol might record the site or investigation reference. Keep mobile response notes within approved operational record procedures.
Our third option is unavailable maintenance, with the unavailable meaning and a required note. This makes an equipment defect visible without suggesting that the resource remains ready for dispatch. Set the order to 0, 1, and 2, so ready, searching, and unavailable appear predictably. Adding an option to the dialogues table is still an unsaved change. For wild land or search teams, it can distinguish staging and active work from unavailable equipment. More options are useful only if members can select them consistently. A new unit status set needs to be assigned before a unit can use it.
Open types, find the rescue unit type, and choose field response under actions, custom unit statuses. Save the assignment. This changes the status choices for every unit that uses the rescue type in this department. Squad 3 is our example rescue unit. Reopen its status picker and check that ready for assignment, searching assigned area, and unavailable maintenance are present. For a security department, you might assign a patrol status set to its patrol vehicle type.
For an industrial team, separate equipment types can use different operational choices. A type assignment changes the available choices for all units of that type. Changing one unit's current status affects that unit. Select Searching Assigned Area. The destination picker now includes the active training calls because calls was recorded at creation.
